source: University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources, Statewide IPM Program
title: Anthracnose of Strawberry — Pest Management Guidelines
content: Strawberry anthracnose (Colletotrichum species) is managed with clean planting stock, sanitation, resistant cultivars and fungicides. Use certified disease-free transplants from an approved nursery, since the fungus is spread on planting material; plant resistant cultivars where available. Avoid overhead irrigation that spreads spores and prolongs leaf and fruit wetness, and remove and destroy infected plants, runners, fruit and debris promptly. Do not work in wet fields. Apply labelled fungicides on a protectant schedule during the susceptible flowering and fruiting period, alternating multi-site and single-site materials and rotating modes of action to slow resistance. Follow the label for rate, interval, and pre-harvest interval; anthracnose fruit rot requires a tight spray interval under high pressure.
author: University of California Agriculture and Natural Resources (UC ANR) Statewide IPM Program
